title: Attested evidence escrow and fallbacks PRD (rough)
content:
Summary

This document sketches a proposal for producing compact attested evidence artifacts for customer managed networks and defining an ordered set of fallback delivery channels and degraded approval policies. The goal is to keep customer change velocity high while preserving a verifiable audit trail even when primary telemetry is blocked or intermittent.

Problem statement

Many Private customers run restricted egress, air gapped segments, or conditional peering to control plane endpoints. Our current approval and audit assumptions require near real time ingestion. When ingestion fails we either block changes or allow them without adequate evidence. Both outcomes are unacceptable for regulated customers.

High level goals

- Define a small, attested evidence artifact that captures essential facts about a change and can be verified later. Target typical size under 64KB and an upper allowed bound of 256KB.
- Design an ordered fallback delivery model with clear delivery assertions.
- Specify degraded approval modes with conservative defaults and customer override knobs.
- Provide operator tooling to inspect outstanding evidence and perform safe rescue actions.
- Ensure forensic replay and signature verification for post hoc audits.

Artifact outline and signing model

We propose an attested evidence artifact that contains a small set of textual fields and compact references to larger blobs. The artifact records the change id, requester identity, timestamps, list of affected resources as identifiers, short diff pointers, an ordered list of approval stamps, and a cryptographic digest plus a signature. The artifact is machine readable but also short enough for email or SFTP transfer in constrained environments. Signing can be done by the agent sidecar or by the control plane depending on KMS availability. The artifact includes a canonical serialization format to avoid signature ambiguity.

Delivery and escrow fallbacks

Primary channel: control plane ingest over TLS when reachable.
Fallbacks in order: agent to customer SIEM if configured and reachable; host local encrypted escrow with configurable replication across N local stores; automated out of band push to a configured security mailbox or approved transfer endpoint; and lastly a human readable evidence card that operators can export and deliver manually.

Each delivery attempt must create a small delivery assertion record that notes the artifact id, the channel used, a channel timestamp, and the channel identifier. Delivery assertions are searchable metadata points that form a chain of custody.

Degraded approval policies

We define several operating modes with conservative defaults: normal, degraded conditional, and emergency forced. For each mode we enumerate permitted actions, required number of approval stamps, any escrow requirements, wait windows, and automatic escalation behavior. Example conservative defaults include allowing rollbacks and read only maintenance in degraded conditional mode when a local escrow replica exists and at least two operator stamps are present. Emergency forced mode permits immediate fixes but marks the change with a short mandatory evidence delivery window and a configurable rollback trigger if evidence is not ingested within a threshold.

Operator UX and tooling

Console features: per change id view showing artifact digest, latest delivery assertions, and recommended remediation steps when evidence is missing. Widgets to produce a short evidence export and to trigger automated retry of fallback channels.

CLI features: commands to query artifact status, export a human readable evidence summary, and perform controlled emergency approvals. All CLI outputs include clear links or instructions for further forensic validation.

Forensic verification and replay

Artifacts must be verifiable by recomputing canonical digests and validating signatures against the expected keys. We will provide a small verification and replay utility that can rehydrate diffs from referenced snapshots when customer snapshots are available and validate pre and post condition checks recorded in the artifact.

Operational constraints and acceptance criteria

- Artifact creation should be designed to not exceed 150 milliseconds added latency in the synchronous approval path; async artifact generation is allowed where callers opt out.
- In constrained network simulations the primary plus fallback paths must produce at least one delivery assertion in 95 percent of runs.
- Console and CLI surfaces must make outstanding evidence obvious and provide one click or one command rescue operations.

Implementation milestones (rough)

1. Finalize artifact canonical form and minimal field set, including delivery assertion schema. 2 weeks.
2. Build reference agent sidecar that produces artifacts and local escrow behavior. 4 to 6 weeks.
3. Implement ingest API and delivery assertion store in control plane. 3 weeks.
4. Console and CLI status and rescue flows. 3 to 4 weeks.
5. Fallback connectors: email reference forwarder and SFTP push, plus a SIEM adapter. 3 weeks.
6. Compliance review and acceptance tests. 2 to 3 weeks.

Acceptance test examples

- Simulate blocked control plane egress and verify artifacts are produced, persisted to local escrow, and a delivery assertion is present.
- Force delayed ingestion and verify emergency mode triggers any configured rollback and alerts.
- Run forensic replay to validate end to end signature verification and diff rehydration when snapshots are provided.

Open questions for review

- Legal review to confirm acceptability of email or transferred signed artifacts as evidence for regulated customers.
- KMS model choice for signing artifacts and whether we allow mixed signing strategies.
- Cost and retention defaults for control plane storage and for local escrow; potential customer configuration options and pricing implications.

Next steps and asks

- Ask legal to review evidence acceptance model and provide recommended wording for audit contracts.
- Engineering to kick off small RFC to lock artifact schema and signature canonicalization.
- SRE to validate retention and cost model for recommended defaults.

End of document
